rationale: Surge rose 1.0x -> 1.6x and the notice ("Demand is high near you, so fares are now 1.6× the usual rate. Your new estimated fare is $15.91.") did not state a free-cancel option: not notified under SURGE-1 -> refund the surge differential (SURGE-2). Differential = (1.6 − 1.0) × surgeable subtotal $8.63 = $5.18; the booking fee is not surged (SURGE-3). The fare is only $4.65 above the quote (the trip ran shorter than the estimate), so the refund is capped at $4.65. A fraud flag raises the bar to 95% (TH-3). The outcome rests on reading the notice text; a lone reading gives 87%. Settled by agreement (both sides read it the same way) -> refund_partial $4.65; otherwise a person decides.
